original_question: If a finite lattice has n join-irreducible elements, what is the largest possible number f(n) of meet-irreducible elements it can have?
target_in_paper: Section 2 ("Problems of 2025"), Problem 18: the notebook records Stanley's Chapter 3, Exercise 29 asking for the extremal number of meet-irreducible elements in a finite lattice with a prescribed number of join-irreducibles.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct object (finite lattices), the correct parameters (number of join-irreducible versus meet-irreducible elements), and the correct extremal task (maximize the latter as a function of the former). It stays very close to the actual problem listed in the paper.
missing_details: The quantifier should be explicit: for each integer n>=1, define an extremal function over all finite lattices with exactly n join-irreducible elements.

To be stand-alone, the standard meanings of join-irreducible and meet-irreducible should be stated (in a finite lattice: join-irreducible means covering exactly one element; meet-irreducible means being covered by exactly one element).
It should explicitly say that f(n) is the maximum of |M(L)| over all finite lattices L with |J(L)|=n, rather than leaving the universe of optimization implicit.

The paper adds no extra hypotheses such as distributive, modular, graded, atomic, or semimodular; those exclusions should remain explicit in the refined version by not introducing any such restrictions.
refined_question:
For each integer n >= 1, let f(n) be the maximum possible number of meet-irreducible elements of a finite lattice L with exactly n join-irreducible elements; equivalently,

f(n)=max\{|M(L)| : L \text{ is a finite lattice and } |J(L)|=n\},

where J(L) and M(L) denote the sets of join-irreducible and meet-irreducible elements of L, respectively (so in a finite lattice, join-irreducible means covering exactly one element and meet-irreducible means being covered by exactly one element). Determine f(n).
justification: The supplied arXiv paper is a notebook of open problems rather than a single-aim research article. The relevant target is Problem 18 in Section 2, which points directly to Stanley's Enumerative Combinatorics, Volume 1, Chapter 3, Exercise 29. The paper's formulation is terse and does not impose any additional structural assumptions on the lattice, so the faithful stand-alone refinement is simply to define the extremal function explicitly and spell out the standard finite-lattice meanings of join-irreducible and meet-irreducible. Your draft is already very close; the main improvement is making the maximization domain and the operator definitions explicit.
